newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan opposition disrupts budget speech.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan opposition disrupts budget speech.

text.p: Kenyan opposition members of parliament disrupted Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi's budget speech on Thursday with noisy demands for constitutional reforms.
Mudavadi was beginning his thirteenth attempt to be heard above the din when state television suspended its live coverage of the parliament's session.
Waving banners saying "No Reforms, No Budget", the opposition parliamentarians stamped their feet and shouted, drowning out Mudavadi's speech.
President Daniel arap Moi, who is also a member of parliament, watched the chaotic scenes from the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) benches.
The speaker, Francis Ole Kaparo, repeatedly cried "Order, Order" and appealed to the opposition to stop their protest.
Kaparo earlier refused opposition member James Orengo's request for a debate on proposed constitutional reforms before elections at an unspecified date later this year.
The government had thrown a thick security blanket over central Nairobi since early morning to prevent a planned opposition demonstration outside parliament.
